chapter: Second day: early memories, London 1966 and other singers
title: Victoria Spivey finds her for the London blues festival
summary: Spivey and Lenny Kunstadt locate her in Detroit; Willie Dixon arranges the trip to London after her boyfriend Buddy objects.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How did it feel when you went to Europe to be in that blues festival?

Well, they wanted a star over there and they had two shows over there. So this man wasn't going to with it no more. So call on my telephone, we told him to call on my telephone, say, "I found Sippie Wallace." I was going to rehearsal to my
choir and when I went, (unintelligible)-- Who called you, Ms. Wallace? Who called you? Was it Victoria?
She visited my house, she visited me.
Oh, she was visiting you.
She called my sister and she always would visit me .
In Detroit.

In Detroit. She would always come from Brooklyn to visit me here. So she come -- I don't know how Victoria found me, but when she come, she -- and some kind of way, she found me. Some kind of way, she found me. And she went to -- come to my house and she say, "Sippie, you could go to London. They wants a blues singer in London." And the man I was going with named Buddy, his name's Buddy, and so I asked Buddy (unintelligible) go to London, I was going. I wasn't Buddy.
Sure.
(Unintelligible).
(Laughter.)

That's true. He didn't want me to go, child. (Unintelligible) on the telephone, say, "William? I found Sippie." So we talked on the telephone. He said, "Are you sure that's Sippie?" He said, "Oh, yeah, (unintelligible). Yeah, this is Sippie, all right." He said, "If you're sure,

then we'll talk with her." And so then he (unintelligible) tell me about going to London. And so he was supposed to send me the money to come to Chicago to leave Sunday going to London. So the money didn't come. So I don't know where I got it from, but everybody say, "If you want to go, you go to London yourself -- go to Chicago yourself."
Didn't Victoria want to go?
No, she had been and I thought Vicky would go -- I thought she was going to London, but no, she had been the year before then.
Oh, I see. So they wanted somebody new.
New.
How did that feel for you to be on the stage and such a big hit?
I was scared to death, I was scared to death.
You were?
You know I was scared. And Vicky didn't go (unintelligible). Vicky didn't make the date. And so they sent for me. And if I hadn't made the date, well, they would call it a day for the performance.
Well, wasn't that fun for you to be a star again?
